title: Clemson women's lacrosse ranked fifth; Shurtleff and Macleod named preseason All-ACC - Upstate SC News
text:
Clemson, S.C. – The Atlantic Coast Conference (ACC) has released its preseason coaches poll and All-ACC team for women’s lacrosse, with Clemson ranked fifth in the league. Two Clemson players, Natalie Shurtleff and Kayla Macleod, were named to the preseason All-ACC squad.
Shurtleff, a midfielder, is Clemson’s all-time points leader with 99 points. She also ranks second in career assists with 41 and holds the second-most assists in a season for the program (21 in 2025), tied for third-most (20 in 2024). Shurtleff is tied for fourth on Clemson’s career goals list and is two goals away from entering the top three. She shares sixth place for most points in a season with Macleod (57 in 2025) and ranks tenth (42 in 2024). Her achievements include eighth-most goals in a season (36 in 2025), sharing the program record for most assists in a game (four against Virginia Tech on April 5, 2025), sixth place in career ground balls (46), fifth place in career draw controls (69), tenth place for single-season draw controls (35 in 2025), seventh place for career turnovers (23), tied for second-most career game-winning goals (three, including two last season), and fourth place for career free-position goals (13).
Macleod ranks second all-time at Clemson with 90 career points. She shares sixth place with Shurtleff for most points in a season (57 in 2025) and holds the program record for most goals scored with 77, including a single-season high of 47 last year. Macleod is tied with Regan Byrne and two others for second-most goals scored in a game by a Tiger player (six). She also ties eighth on Clemson’s all-time assist list with 13 assists. Macleod leads the program with 15 woman-up goals—six more than any other player—and holds the record for most woman-up goals scored by an individual during one season at Clemson, netting ten last year. Alongside teammates Blair Byrne and Shurtleff as well as two others, she is tied for second-most career game-winning goals at three. Additionally, she has set a program record of 26 free position goals over her career.
Fans can follow updates about Clemson women’s lacrosse through their official accounts on X, Instagram, and Facebook.
